name: Normal Ray Alignment Loss
definition: A regularization loss that encourages predicted normals at sample points to align or anti-align with the ray direction, useful for orienting normals toward or away from the camera.
summary: Normal Ray Alignment Loss is a regularization term that enforces geometric consistency by aligning predicted surface normals with viewing rays, distinguishing itself from Curvature Loss by optimizing the dot product rather than penalizing smoothness.
